cards.title: THE HOME OFFICE
cards.tagline: SIX ZONES. START WITH THE DESK.
cards.objective: The home office is six small jobs built around one shared trap: physical clutter and unmade decisions about paper. This card is the map and the order.
cards.start_here: HOZ-001 Primary Desk. Clear the desk surface completely before you open a single drawer. Every other zone in this room gets emptied onto that surface at some point, so it has to be the first thing finished and the last thing you let refill.
how_to_play: 1. Deal the six ZONE cards face up. Pick the one that is annoying you today, or take the one this card says to start at.
2. Lay out that zone's three FRICTION cards. Keep the ones that are true in your home office. Put the rest back.
3. Turn a friction card over and pick the answer that is true. It names a ROOT CAUSE.
4. The root cause card names the ACTION cards that fix that cause. Pick the one that matches the time you actually have: fifteen or thirty minutes.
5. Do it standing up, with the card in your hand.
6. Read the victory condition out loud. If it is not true yet, you are not finished, and that is the whole scoring system.
7. Fill in the zone's STANDARD card with a pen and put it where the zone is.
8. Draw an EVENT card when an ordinary hard day happens, and see whether the standard held.
cards.players: 1 to 6. With more than one, split the chain: one clears the desk and drawers, another works the filing and the shelf.
cards.six_s: Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain
cards.safety_first: Do HOA-015 The Quarterly Reach-Behind Clean and Safety Walk before any rebuild. It takes thirty minutes and covers the cables, the cabinets, the shelves and the printer.

cards.title: PRIMARY DESK
cards.tagline: ONE INBOX TRAY. UNDER A DOZEN SHEETS, ALWAYS.

safety_checks.question: Water and electricity
safety_checks.text: A mug of coffee sitting behind the keyboard on the same surface as a power strip and a laptop charger. Move drinks to the far side of the mouse, away from cables and the machine.

safety_checks.question: Fall
safety_checks.text: Charger cables and the power strip lead running across the floor where the chair moves and where you push back to stand.

the_call.title: The half-finished thing
the_call.text: One corner of the desk is held by a project you have not touched in weeks and cannot put away, because putting it away feels like admitting it is over. Say the next physical action out loud in one sentence. If you can name it ("call the insurer", "sign page four"), it is live: write that sentence on a card, clip it to the papers, and it goes in the inbox tray, not on the desk. If you cannot name a next action, it is not stalled, it is abandoned. Box it, write today's date on the lid, put it on the shelf, and if the box is still unopened on that date next year, it leaves unopened.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: Loose scissors and a letter opener rolling free in a drawer you reach into without looking, and a pedestal that tips forward if you pull the loaded file drawer fully out while the top drawer is open.

the_call.title: The cable bag
the_call.text: Somewhere in the pedestal there is a bag or a drawer of cables, adapters, and wall bricks, and it survives because each individual cable is too cheap to think about and too specific to throw away. That decision cannot be made one cable at a time. Empty the whole lot onto the desk at once, pick up each cable, name the device it powers, and point at where that device physically is in this house. No device, no keep. Then keep exactly one spare of each connector type you still use daily, coil and band it, and take the rest to electronics recycling this week. Made in one batch at the cleared desk, it is a single sitting. Made one cable at a time, it never gets made at all.

cards.title: FILE STORAGE
cards.tagline: ONE QUESTION PER FOLDER. ONE STRAIGHT LINE OF TABS.
cards.objective: Keep the documents you are genuinely required to hold, and put your hand on any one of them without opening a second drawer.
callouts: Hanging folders labeled by the question you would ask
Every tab in the same position along the row

The cabinet anchored to the wall

safety_checks.question: Burn or fire
safety_checks.text: A four-drawer cabinet of dense paper standing against a heater, or the overflow boxes stacked on top of a power strip. Paper is the fuel load of this room, so keep it clear of heat and of the outlet.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: A tall filing cabinet will tip forward onto you if the top drawer is loaded and pulled fully out. Anchor it to the wall and open one drawer at a time.

the_call.title: What you are actually required to keep
the_call.text: Most of this drawer is neither obviously permanent nor obviously rubbish, and that middle band is why the whole job stalls. Split it into three by rule. Permanent originals, meaning birth and marriage certificates, deeds, vehicle titles, wills, and immigration papers, go into one closed fireproof box and never into the filing cabinet. Tax returns and their supporting paper get one folder per year and are held for whatever your local retention period is, which you look up once and write on the card. Everything else, the bank statements, the utility bills, the receipts for things you no longer own, goes by this test: if the issuer will reprint it on request, or it already lives inside an online account, it is information, not a record, and information does not get a folder.

the_call.title: The shelf that says who you used to be
the_call.text: The textbooks from a degree, the professional library from a job you left, the reference set that a website now answers better and faster. These are the hardest books in the house to release, because they stand for a version of you that you have not formally retired. The rule that settles it: ask when you last took it down since it arrived on this shelf, not whether you might one day. If you cannot name a specific occasion, and the book is one you could borrow or reorder inside a week, it is no longer reference, it is display, and it must now win a display slot in open competition with everything else on the shelf. Most of them will not. Appliance manuals are simpler: model still in the house, keep it; model gone, it goes today.

cards.title: PRINTER AND SCANNING STATION

safety_checks.question: Burn or fire
safety_checks.text: A laser printer pushed tight against the wall or into a closed cupboard with no clearance behind it, and powered through a strip plugged into another strip. The fuser needs air and the machine needs its own wall outlet.

safety_checks.question: Water and electricity
safety_checks.text: A plant or a water glass sitting on top of the printer lid, directly above the electronics and the paper path.

the_call.title: The backup printer
the_call.text: The old printer is still in the corner, or on the floor of the cupboard, because it might be a backup. Settle it before you leave this corner today: plug it in and print a test page right now. If it prints, and you are prepared to keep a spare cartridge for it in stock, it is a backup and it gets a home. If you will not plug it in today, it is not a backup, it is a large object you have not decided about, and it goes to electronics recycling this week. Apply the same blade to the sealed cartridges: hold each box against the model number on the machine you actually use. Anything unmatched sells this week for more than it will ever be worth again, because cartridge value only falls.

cards.tagline: ONE OPEN PACK. ONE SPARE BEHIND IT. NOTED ON THE SHELF.

safety_checks.question: Fall
safety_checks.text: Reaching the top shelf from a rolling office chair. The chair moves under you the moment you shift your weight, so bring a step stool into this room and keep it here.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: Reams of paper and boxes of envelopes stored above shoulder height, where a slipping box lands on your head and shoulders while your arms are up.

the_call.title: The deal you got
the_call.text: The bulk box of 500 envelopes, the multipack of sticky notes, the case of paper bought because the price was good. The genuinely hard part is that you were not wrong about the price, and admitting the surplus was a mistake feels like throwing money away twice. It is not: the money left when you bought it, and the shelf space is being paid for now. Count the true stock and divide it by your honest annual use, out loud. Six letters a year against 500 envelopes is a lifetime supply and then some. Cap it at one open plus one spare of anything you use monthly, and a single year of use for everything else. The surplus goes to a school, a charity shop, or a neighbour this week. Not to the top shelf, and not to a box in the garage.

cards.tagline: WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE. THEN WHY.
cards.objective: Reaching into this cabinet is awkward or unsafe.

branches.answer: Reams of paper are stored above shoulder height
The step stool lives in another room, so a chair gets stood on instead
Shelves are so deep things get lost at the back

cards.title: EXCESS
cards.objective: More things are kept here than the zone's job needs.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Count what you used in the past month. If the honest number is a third of what is stored here, the space is not too small.
cards.instruction: This is a Sort problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a shelf crowded with far more identical pens or notebooks than one desk could ever use
must_show: More things are kept here than the zone's job needs.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: NO ASSIGNED HOME
cards.objective: The thing has no single defined destination, so it lands wherever the hand opens.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask where one specific item lives. If two people answer differently, or nobody answers, it has no home.
cards.instruction: This is a Straighten problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a loose cable and a notepad lying on a desk with no drawer, tray or hook anywhere near them

cards.title: WRONG LOCATION
cards.objective: It is stored somewhere, just not where it is used.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Stand where you use it and count the steps to where it is kept. More than two is the wrong cabinet.
cards.instruction: This is a Straighten problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a stack of cardboard boxes stored directly under a desk where a chair needs to roll
must_show: It is stored somewhere, just not where it is used.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: EXCESS MOTION
cards.objective: Getting it out means bending, lifting, unstacking, or moving something else first: too many steps.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Fetch it once and count the movements. More than two and the storage is charging you rent every time.
cards.instruction: This is a Straighten problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a notebook sitting on a shelf across the room, out of arm's reach from the desk chair
must_show: Getting it out means bending, lifting, unstacking, or moving something else first: too many steps.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: POOR VISIBILITY
cards.objective: You own it, but you cannot see it, so you buy it again or forget it.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Open the door and, without moving anything, name what is at the back. If you cannot, that stock is invisible.
cards.instruction: This is a Straighten problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a row of hanging file folders with tabs staggered at different heights, one folder's tab hidden behind another
must_show: You own it, but you cannot see it, so you buy it again or forget it.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: POOR ACCESSIBILITY
cards.objective: The people who use it cannot reach it safely, or at all.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Have the shortest person who uses this zone fetch what they need daily. If they climb, reach overhead, or ask for help, the height is wrong.
cards.instruction: This is a Safety problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a supply shelf set deep enough that a hand reaching in cannot see or feel what is at the back
must_show: The people who use it cannot reach it safely, or at all.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: INSUFFICIENT CAPACITY
cards.objective: The right storage exists and genuinely cannot hold what belongs in it.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Put back only what belongs here. If it still will not close, or still stacks four deep, the capacity is the problem, not the habit.
cards.instruction: This is a Sort problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a drawer stuffed so full that a folder springs up the moment the drawer opens
must_show: The right storage exists and genuinely cannot hold what belongs in it.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: MISSING STANDARD
cards.objective: Nobody agreed what good looks like, so everybody is right.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask two people what this surface should look like at bedtime. Two answers means there is no standard to keep.
cards.instruction: This is a Standardize problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: one drawer holding pens, paper clips and tape all mixed with no divider between them
must_show: Nobody agreed what good looks like, so everybody is right.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: MISSING TRIGGER
cards.objective: The reset is a good intention with nothing to attach it to.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Name the moment it happens. If the answer is "when I get round to it", there is no trigger and it will not survive a bad week.
cards.instruction: This is a Sustain problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: an inbox tray stacked well past a dozen sheets, no calendar or clock nearby marking when it was last cleared
must_show: The reset is a good intention with nothing to attach it to.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: SAFETY CONSTRAINT
cards.objective: The current arrangement can hurt somebody, and that outranks tidy.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Look for the four: a blade your hand would meet, weight above shoulder height, heat beside something that burns, and an unsafe placement near a child's reach.
cards.instruction: This is a Safety problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a pair of scissors lying blade-up and loose in an open desk drawer
must_show: The current arrangement can hurt somebody, and that outranks tidy.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: POOR REPLENISHMENT
cards.objective: Consumables run out unnoticed, and stock ages out of use unseen.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Find the last one of something you use daily. If nothing tells you it is the last one, you will find out at the worst possible moment.
cards.instruction: This is a Standardize problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: an empty box of paper clips sitting back on the shelf where a full one used to be
must_show: Consumables run out unnoticed, and stock ages out of use unseen.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: UNCLEAR OWNERSHIP
cards.objective: Nobody specific is responsible for resetting this zone, so upkeep depends on whoever notices first.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask who resets this zone. If the honest answer is "whoever gets to it" or two names with no agreement, there is no owner.
cards.instruction: This is a Sustain problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: an empty printer paper bin standing untouched with nobody nearby to refill it
must_show: Nobody specific is responsible for resetting this zone, so upkeep depends on whoever notices first.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: UNRESOLVED DECISION
cards.objective: The item is not clutter, it is a decision that has not been made, so it is stacked instead of acted on.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Pick up one piece. If your first thought is a verb (pay, sign, call, decide) rather than a place, it needs a decision, not a home.
cards.instruction: This is a Sort problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a single loose sheet of paper sitting alone on an otherwise cleared desk corner
must_show: The item is not clutter, it is a decision that has not been made, so it is stacked instead of acted on.
art.accept_test: One idea, one object, no room tour. If the picture could illustrate three different causes it is rejected.

cards.title: DIFFICULT TO CLEAN
cards.objective: Reaching the surface to clean it costs more effort than the rest of the zone combined, so it gets skipped.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Time how long it actually takes to reach and wipe the surface. If it requires moving something first, that cost is why it is skipped.
cards.instruction: This is a Shine problem. Draw one of the action cards listed and do it now, at the length you actually have.

art.subject: a hand reaching behind a printer into a narrow gap tight against the wall

cards.title: CLEAR THE DESK AND HOOK THE STRIP UP
cards.objective: Clear the desk down to the monitor, keyboard and mouse, and get the power strip off the floor.
cards.why_it_matters: Paper with no other place to land is why this desk fills back up by the end of the week, and a power strip on the floor is what the chair catches on every time.
inputs: nothing beyond fifteen minutes and the inbox tray
steps: Take everything off the desk except the monitor, keyboard and mouse. Put the loose paper into the inbox tray, give every sheet in it a verdict until it is under a dozen, and hook the power strip up off the floor.
Set the notebook on your writing-hand side and the phone face down beyond it.
Check the sweep the mouse travels is left completely bare.
cards.victory_condition: One notebook and one tray under a dozen sheets, and the chair rolls the width of the desk without catching.

art.subject: a desk with only the monitor, keyboard and mouse on it, a notebook and a small inbox tray beside it holding fewer than a dozen sheets, and a power strip hooked onto the desk leg clear of the floor
must_show: One notebook and one tray under a dozen sheets, and the chair rolls the width of the desk without catching.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: PHOTOGRAPH THE CLEARED DESK
cards.objective: Photograph the cleared desk, tape the print inside the drawer, and settle the half-finished project sitting in the corner.
cards.why_it_matters: A surface with no photographed standard drifts back to full by familiarity alone, not volume, and a project you cannot name a next action for is not stalled, it is abandoned.
inputs: a printer or tape for the photo
steps: Clear the desk completely and photograph it.
Tape the printed photo inside the top drawer so the word clear stops being a matter of opinion.
Say the half-finished project's next physical action out loud in one sentence; if you can name it, write it on a card and clip it into the inbox tray.
If you cannot name a next action, box the project, mark today's date on the lid, and put it on the shelf.
cards.victory_condition: A taped photo of the bare desk hangs inside the drawer, and the half-finished project either carries a named next action or sits boxed and dated on the shelf.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a photograph of a bare desk taped inside an open desk drawer, a small labelled box with a dated marking on its lid sitting on a shelf nearby
must_show: A taped photo of the bare desk hangs inside the drawer, and the half-finished project either carries a named next action or sits boxed and dated on the shelf.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: TEST THE PENS AND SLOT THE SCISSORS
cards.objective: Empty the top drawer, test every pen, and give the scissors a fixed point-down slot.
cards.why_it_matters: A drawer you reach into without looking is the wrong place for a loose blade, and a dead pen that goes back in the drawer is a decision deferred, not avoided.
steps: Empty the top drawer, test every pen on a scrap and bin the ones that skip, then put back only what writes into a divided tray with the scissors point-down in their own slot.
Wipe the tray before anything goes back into it.
Confirm the stapler sits in the tray, not riding on top of any folder.
cards.victory_condition: Every pen in the drawer writes first time, and the scissors have a slot of their own.

art.subject: an open desk drawer with a divided tray holding only pens that write, a stapler in its own compartment, and scissors resting point-down in a dedicated slot
must_show: Every pen in the drawer writes first time, and the scissors have a slot of their own.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: EMPTY THE CABLE BAG
cards.objective: Empty the whole bag of loose cables and adapters onto the desk, name each device, and keep one spare of each connector you actually use.
cards.why_it_matters: A drawer full of cables too cheap to think about and too specific to throw away only clears when the whole bag is judged at once, not one cable at a time.
inputs: a labelled small box for the kept spares
steps: Empty the whole cable bag onto the cleared desk in one go.
Pick up each cable and adapter and point at the device it powers, physically, somewhere in this house.
Anything with no device gets no keep: it goes straight into the recycling bag.
Coil and band exactly one spare of each connector type you still use daily, and box the rest for electronics recycling this week.
cards.victory_condition: One labelled box holds exactly one spare of each connector type still in daily use, and everything else is boxed for electronics recycling.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a small labelled box holding one coiled spare of each cable connector type, a bag of surplus adapters set aside for electronics recycling nearby
must_show: One labelled box holds exactly one spare of each connector type still in daily use, and everything else is boxed for electronics recycling.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: RELABEL ONE DRAWER BY THE QUESTION
cards.objective: Relabel one drawer's folders by the question you would ask, and line up every tab.
cards.why_it_matters: Nobody has ever gone looking for a folder called Correspondence, and a staggered row of tabs makes your eye zigzag instead of run straight down the line.
inputs: blank tab inserts or a marker
steps: Take one drawer. Relabel each folder with the question you would ask when looking for it, set every tab in the same position, and shred the statements you could download again.
Check the drawer closes without pressure once the tabs are aligned.
Carry anything shredded straight to the bag by the door.
cards.victory_condition: One drawer where the tabs read down in a single line, and it closes without pressure.

art.subject: an open filing cabinet drawer with folder tabs relabelled and standing in a single straight line, the drawer closing easily with room to spare
must_show: One drawer where the tabs read down in a single line, and it closes without pressure.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: SORT INTO KEEP, SCAN, SHRED
cards.objective: Work the backlog pile into three piles by rule, and get the retention card written.
cards.why_it_matters: The middle band, neither obviously permanent nor obviously rubbish, is why this job stalls; a rule applied once settles the whole pile instead of one sheet at a time.
inputs: a scanner if you keep digital copies
an index card for the retention rule
steps: Work one drawer at a time into three piles: keep as paper, scan then shred, shred now.
Move permanent originals into a closed fireproof box, never the filing cabinet.
Write your retention rule on a card and tape it inside the top drawer.
Carry the finished shred pile straight to the bag by the door.
cards.victory_condition: Every sheet from the drawer sits in one of three piles, permanent originals are in the fireproof box, and the retention card is taped inside the drawer.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: three piles of paper on a desk marked by role, keep, scan, and shred, a small fireproof box standing to one side and a retention card visible taped inside an open drawer
must_show: Every sheet from the drawer sits in one of three piles, permanent originals are in the fireproof box, and the retention card is taped inside the drawer.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: MOVE THE WEIGHT DOWN AND ANCHOR THE SHELF
cards.objective: Move the heaviest binders down, bring real reference to eye level, and confirm the wall fixing.
cards.why_it_matters: An unanchored shelf loaded heavy at the top is a fall risk the moment you pull the wrong book, and reference you cannot reach without standing is reference you stop using.
inputs: a wall anchor kit if none is fitted
steps: Move every heavy binder to the bottom two shelves, bring the reference you actually open to seated eye level, then check the wall fixing and fit one if it is missing.
Close each group with a bookend.
Confirm a hand's width of empty shelf remains at the end of every row.
cards.victory_condition: The heaviest things are lowest, the unit does not move when you pull a book, and every row ends in a hand's width of space.

art.subject: a bookshelf with heavy binders moved to the bottom two shelves, working reference books at seated eye level closed off with a bookend, and a visible wall anchor strap securing the top of the unit
must_show: The heaviest things are lowest, the unit does not move when you pull a book, and every row ends in a hand's width of space.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: THIN ONE GROUP BY THE LAST-TAKEN-DOWN TEST
cards.objective: For one group of books, name the last time each was taken down, and remove anything that fails the test.
cards.why_it_matters: A book that stands for who you used to be is the hardest to release, and the shelf only stays a working shelf if reference wins its place in open competition with everything else on it.
inputs: a box for books leaving the house
steps: Pick one group of books on the shelf.
For each one, name out loud a specific occasion you last took it down; if you cannot, it is display, not reference.
Box anything that fails the test for donation or resale.
Confirm a hand's width of empty shelf remains once the group is thinned.
cards.victory_condition: Every book in the group has a named reason for staying, and a hand's width of shelf is free at the end of the row.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a bookshelf group with several books removed and boxed for donation, the remaining books standing with clear space at the end of the row
must_show: Every book in the group has a named reason for staying, and a hand's width of shelf is free at the end of the row.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: DRAW THE MIN LINE AND CLEAR THE VENTS
cards.objective: Clear the space around the printer and mark a min and max line on the paper bin.
cards.why_it_matters: A printer with no clear air behind it and no visible paper level is how this room runs out mid-job and overheats at the same time.
steps: Clear the top of and the space behind the printer, draw a min line and a max line on the paper bin, and split the scan tray into a to-do side and a done side.
Move anything sitting on top of the lid off it for good.
Confirm the printer plugs straight into a wall outlet, not a strip chained off another strip.
cards.victory_condition: Air behind the machine, a paper level anyone can read at a glance, and a scan tray that says what still needs doing.

art.subject: a printer with a paper bin marked with a min line and a max line beneath it, clear space visible behind the machine, and a scan tray split into a to-do side and a done side
must_show: Air behind the machine, a paper level anyone can read at a glance, and a scan tray that says what still needs doing.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: SETTLE THE BACKUP PRINTER AND MATCH THE CARTRIDGES
cards.objective: Test the spare printer for real, decide backup or recycle, and match every cartridge box to the machine you actually use.
cards.why_it_matters: An unplugged spare printer is a large object you have not decided about, not a backup, and an unmatched cartridge only loses value the longer it sits.
inputs: a marker to note the model on kept cartridge boxes
steps: Plug in the spare printer and print a test page right now.
If it prints and you will stock a spare cartridge for it, give it a real home; if not, box it for electronics recycling this week.
Hold every sealed cartridge box against the model number on the machine you actually use.
Sell or recycle any cartridge that does not match.
cards.victory_condition: The spare printer either has a real home with a named spare cartridge or is boxed for recycling, and every kept cartridge matches the machine on the desk.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a spare printer either freshly settled onto a shelf with a printed test page beside it or boxed for recycling, a small stack of cartridge boxes matched against a printer's visible model number
must_show: The spare printer either has a real home with a named spare cartridge or is boxed for recycling, and every kept cartridge matches the machine on the desk.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: CONSOLIDATE TO ONE OPEN PACK EACH
cards.objective: Bring every consumable together and consolidate to one open pack of each at hand height.
cards.why_it_matters: A dozen packs of sticky notes look like nothing until they stand side by side, and backstock nobody can see is backstock that gets bought again.
inputs: a card and marker for the min/max note
steps: Bring every consumable together, move reams to the bottom shelf, put one open pack of each at hand height with its backstock directly behind, and write min and max on a card inside the door.
Line up the true count of each item where you can see it before deciding what stays.
Recycle dried glue sticks, dead markers and cracked folders now.
cards.victory_condition: One open pack of each thing visible at hand height, nothing heavy above your shoulder, and a card that says when to buy.

art.subject: a supply cabinet shelf with one open pack of each consumable at hand height, its backstock lined up directly behind it, and a card marked with min and max lines taped inside the door
must_show: One open pack of each thing visible at hand height, nothing heavy above your shoulder, and a card that says when to buy.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: MOVE THE WEIGHT DOWN AND BRING IN THE STOOL
cards.objective: Move reams and heavy boxes below shoulder height, and put a real step stool in this room.
cards.why_it_matters: A rolling chair is not a ladder, and a slipping box from a shoulder-height shelf lands on your head while your arms are already up.
steps: Move every ream of paper and heavy box down to the bottom shelf.
Bring an actual step stool into this room and leave it standing in the corner.
Confirm nothing heavier than light supplies sits above shoulder height.
Check the deepest shelf for anything lost at the back now that reach is easier.
cards.victory_condition: A step stool stands in the corner, and nothing heavier than light supplies sits above shoulder height.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a step stool standing in the corner of a supply room, heavy reams of paper stacked on the bottom shelf, and only light supplies visible above shoulder height
must_show: A step stool stands in the corner, and nothing heavier than light supplies sits above shoulder height.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: FOLLOW ONE PIECE OF PAPER FROM DOOR TO DRAWER
cards.objective: Pick one real piece of paper that arrived today and walk it through every decision point in this room until it lands in a folder or the bin.
cards.why_it_matters: This room's whole job is unmade decisions about paper living in one drawer, and no single zone can be judged in isolation from the others it feeds.
inputs: one real piece of paper that arrived today
steps: Pick up the newest piece of paper that arrived in this room today.
Give it a verdict at the desk: act, file, or recycle, the same test the inbox tray uses.
If it needs filing, carry it straight to the cabinet and give it a folder named for the question you would ask.
If a step along the way stalled, note which zone stalled it: that zone is today's real job, not this one.
cards.victory_condition: The one piece of paper reaches a folder or the bin, and you can name which zone, if any, slowed it down.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a single sheet of paper being carried from a desk inbox tray directly to a labelled folder in an open filing cabinet drawer, no other paper visible along the way
must_show: The one piece of paper reaches a folder or the bin, and you can name which zone, if any, slowed it down.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: THE HOLDING PEN SWEEP
cards.objective: Walk the whole room and carry out anything that is not actually office work.
cards.why_it_matters: This is the room with a door that closes, so it quietly becomes the household's holding pen, and anything that is not office work becomes permanent furniture if it stays past today.
inputs: nothing beyond fifteen minutes and somewhere else in the house to carry things to
steps: Walk every surface and the floor, and name each object: office work, or not.
Carry anything that is not office work to the room it actually belongs in, right now.
If nothing else in the house claims it, box it for donation rather than setting it back down here.
cards.victory_condition: Every object left in the room is genuinely office work.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a home office with a broken lamp, an unopened moving box and a bag of miscellaneous items being carried out through the open door, the room behind them holding only office furniture
must_show: Every object left in the room is genuinely office work.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: THE QUARTERLY REACH-BEHIND CLEAN AND SAFETY WALK
cards.objective: Clean the spots this room hides behind its furniture, and walk it once checking for the four things that hurt people here.
cards.why_it_matters: Dust settles behind the printer and the bookshelf where nobody looks, and water, electricity, a fall and a tipping cabinet are the four risks in this room that only show up if you look on purpose.
inputs: nothing beyond thirty minutes and a working set of hands
steps: Ease the printer, the bookshelf and the filing cabinet out or reach behind each with the crevice tool, and clear the dust and any stray paper.
Check every charger cable and the power strip for a frayed lead or a cable crossing where the chair rolls.
Check the filing cabinet and bookshelf are both anchored, and that nothing heavy sits above head height on either.
Check the scissors and letter opener sit point-down in their own slot, and that the printer has clear air behind it.
Fix anything you find right there, or write it on a card in the inbox tray if it needs a tool you do not have to hand.

cards.objective: The desk holds the tools of the current task plus one inbox tray, and nothing else stays there overnight.
cards.trigger: When you close the laptop lid for the day.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Count the sheets in your inbox tray right now, and if it is more than a dozen, give the top three a verdict before you stand up.
Peel every sticky note off the monitor bezel and either act on it now or copy it into the notebook.
Check the power strip is still hooked on the desk leg, and coil any cable that crosses where the chair rolls.

must_show: the zone holding its standard
art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.title: THE DEADLINE ALL-NIGHTER
cards.objective: A deadline lands and you need the desk and every drawer tool ready for six straight hours of work, starting now.
cards.held_if: The desk is already clear enough to spread out on, and the first pen you grab writes.
cards.if_it_failed: If you had to clear clutter or hunt for a working pen before you could start, the everyday reset was not being kept. Draw HOA-001 or HOA-003.
cards.instruction: Do not do anything to prepare. Live the day, then read the two lines below and be honest about which one you are.

art.accept_test: The pressure has to be visible in the objects. No people, so the load has to be shown by what is on the surfaces.
